bull_bear.body:
- Claims industry leadership and preferred-supplier status with demanding customers on the strength of product quality and long-standing customer relationships, in an industry with numerous SSI/MSME players and intense competition
- Direct relationships with major OEM consumers across static and rotating electrical equipment, auto-electricals, electronics, refrigeration and air-conditioning and consumer durables, supplemented by a dealer channel for small consumers
- Management cites a low debt gearing ratio, good liquidity position and extensive industry experience as the basis for its long-term optimism
- As a matter of policy the company typically engages in back-to-back transactions for copper purchases against finished-goods sales orders, to mitigate raw-material market risk
- Backward integration under way: a Copper Recycling / Refining Project whose cathodes will be used internally to make copper wire rods, the primary raw material for its winding wires
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Copper raw-material availability and price volatility — Copper is the primary raw material; availability during FY 2025-26 was tight globally, prices rose sharply and are stated as likely to remain at elevated levels during FY 2026-27 and prone to sudden fluctuations. Management says this will put pressure on overall finance cost, and mitigates market risk by typically engaging in back-to-back transactions for copper purchases to fulfil finished-goods sales orders.
- Single-product concentration — The MD&A states the Company's core activity is production and sale of only one product, i.e. winding wires made of copper, so demand or margin shocks in that one product flow straight through.
- Trade-receivable recoverability and working-capital concentration — The auditor's Key Audit Matter records aggregate trade receivables at 31 March 2026 of Rs. 92,540.51 lakhs, mostly unsecured and approximately 41.14% of the Company's gross assets - the largest component of the balance sheet, with recoverability reviewed periodically and expected credit loss provided on past record.
- Macro and geo-political demand risk in FY 2026-27 — Management expects the global situation to remain highly volatile and unpredictable - Ukraine war and Iran crisis, US-China tension, reset in US-EU ties, adverse impact of US tariffs, sharp devaluation of the rupee against the USD, much higher oil prices and higher inflation - which could result in lower global and local demand, with domestic copper demand possibly slowing.
- Interest-rate and financing cost risk — Management notes the RBI could be compelled to increase domestic interest rates to control inflation and mitigate exchange outflows, and that global interest rates are likely to go up; elevated copper prices additionally pressure the overall finance cost.
- Supply-chain reconfiguration and disruption — The MD&A states supply chains will continue getting re-configured globally due to the geo-political situation, and lists possible disruptions in global supply chains among the factors making the current year's outlook challenging and likely to increase costs.
- Dependence on the Indian monsoon and domestic macro conditions — Management explicitly states the monsoon will play a big role in the overall performance of the Indian economy during FY 2026-27, on which its domestic demand depends.
- Occupational health and safety / hazardous-material exposure at plants — The BRSR describes hazard identification and risk assessment (HIRA), safety audits, PPE, six-monthly medical examinations and special health check-ups for workers exposed to hazardous chemicals; the safety-incident table reports no fatalities, recordable injuries or LTIFR entries for employees or workers in FY 2025-26 or FY 2024-25.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Precision Wires India Limited manufactures insulated enamelled winding wire of copper and other insulated electric conductors (HS Code 8544, NIC 27320), which accounts for 100% of turnover; the MD&A states the Company's core activity is production and sale of only one product, i.e. Winding Wires made of copper. It caters directly to major OEM consumers making static and rotating electrical equipment, auto-electricals, electronics, refrigeration and air-conditioning and consumer durables, and also serves small consumers through the dealer sector. The BRSR reports 7 plants/operations and 5 offices (including depots) in India, 12 locations in all, serving 18 States and 3 UTs domestically and 22 countries internationally, with exports at 14.83% of total turnover.

outlook.body:
- Focus on prudent and timely capacity enhancements and modernization, quality and process up-gradation, consolidation, rationalization of costs and de-risking of all processes and operations
- Implement a Copper Recycling / Refining Project for copper waste, scrap and un-refined copper, keeping in mind the long-term strategic benefits; the resulting copper cathodes are to be used internally to manufacture copper wire rods, the primary raw material for its copper winding wires
- As a matter of policy, engage in back-to-back transactions for copper purchases to fulfil sales orders for finished goods, to mitigate raw-material market risk
- Retain industry leadership and preferred-supplier status with demanding OEM customers on the basis of product quality and long-standing customer relationships
- Continue a system of reasonably prudent safeguards against the high volatility in raw-material rates and exchange risk
- The Board has formulated and adopted a Dividend Distribution Policy in terms of Regulation 43A of SEBI LODR; the dividend recommendation is stated to be in accordance with that Policy and the dividend will be paid out of the profits for the year. For FY 2025-26 the Company paid two interim dividends and the Board has recommended a final dividend on the Rs. 1/- face-value equity shares, subject to members' approval at the AGM. During FY 2025-26 the Company states it strengthened its capital structure by raising funds through a Preferential Issue on a private placement basis - equity shares and convertible warrants approved by the Board on 17 May 2025 and by members at the EGM of 17 June 2025 - with the warrants converted into equity in October 2025 on receipt of the balance consideration, taking paid-up capital to Rs. 18,28,07,975. The Company confirms it has no subsidiary, associate company or joint venture as on 31.03.2026, so capital is deployed within the standalone entity.
- Occupational Health and Safety management system aligned with ISO 45001:2018 implemented in major plants; the Company's manufacturing units are certified to ISO 45001:2018, covering permanent, temporary and contract workers as well as contractors and subcontractors on Company premises, across all facilities, units, departments, sales offices, branches and operations throughout India
- Structured hazard management: Hazard Identification & Risk Assessment (HIRA), periodic health and safety risk-assessment audits, unit-level Safety Committees, workforce training, regular internal inspections and safety audits, medical examination, emergency preparedness and preventive maintenance/calibration of equipment
- Worker hazard-reporting channels: Whistle Blower and Grievance Redressal policies, Safety Committee meetings, suggestion box, emergency trainings and reporting in the Risk Register
- Health provision: medical examination every six months, special health check-ups for workers exposed to hazardous chemicals, PPE provided to all workers, fire alarms, emergency exits, staircase railings and regular mock drills
- Assessments for the year: 100% of plants and offices assessed on health and safety practices and on working conditions (assessed internally by the Company); 45% of value chain partners by value of business assessed on both
- Life-cover/compensation: employees and workers covered by a compensatory package in the event of death, through a Group Personal Accident policy and ESIC
- Corrective actions underway on safety: SOPs displayed at the workplace, safety training programmes, PPE advisories and written Safe Work Practice instructions made readily available
- The Company states it does not currently offer a transition assistance programme for employees facing career endings, focusing instead on continuously enhancing the skills of existing employees
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The principal expansion project disclosed is a Copper Recycling / Refining Project: keeping in mind the long-term strategic benefits of recycling/refining of copper waste and scrap and un-refined copper, the Company states it is in the process of implementing the project, which will commence operation during FY 2026-27, and that the copper cathodes from it will be used internally for manufacturing copper wire rods - the primary raw material for its copper winding wires. Beyond that named project, the MD&A frames capex only as intent: the Company will focus on prudent and timely capacity enhancements and modernization, quality and process up-gradation, consolidation, rationalization of costs and de-risking of all processes and operations. No commissioning capacity, project cost or ramp profile is stated for the recycling/refining project. The BRSR separately reports R&D and capital-expenditure investments in specific technologies to improve the environmental and social impacts of products and processes as NIL.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Medium and long term, demand for electrical equipment - auto electricals, appliances, air conditioning, refrigeration and the automotive sector - is expected to increase on rising incomes, increasing urbanization and growth in financial, infrastructural and power sectors
- India will continue to invest substantially in infrastructure such as roads, power generation, transmission and distribution and the digital economy, improving connectivity and spurring semi-urban and rural development
- Enhanced energy-efficiency norms for electrical equipment, faster adoption of electric/hybrid vehicle technology, the government's old-vehicle scrapping policy and 'Make in India' incentives make long-term prospects bright
- Government thrust on energy-efficient electrical equipment, energy infrastructure and capacity expansion, and infrastructure investment, would drive long-term growth of the Indian economy and the industry
- Export prospects will improve as western economies may seek to import more from India
- In the medium to longer term the global themes of energy self-sufficiency, energy efficiency and reduction of carbon emissions will play in favour of the industry; electric and hybrid vehicle development in India is at a very early stage but is expected to accelerate significantly during this decade
- Near term (FY 2026-27) the global situation is likely to remain highly volatile and unpredictable - Ukraine war and Iran crisis, US-China tension, reset in US-EU ties, adverse impact of US tariffs, sharp devaluation of the Indian currency v/s USD, much higher oil prices and consequently higher inflation and supply-chain disruptions - which could result in lower global and local demand
- Copper availability during FY 2025-26 was tight globally, prices rose sharply during the year and are likely to remain at elevated levels during FY 2026-27 and prone to sudden fluctuations, putting pressure on overall finance cost
- Domestic demand for copper may slow down, and the monsoon will play a big role in the overall performance of the Indian economy during FY 2026-27
- Volumes during FY 2025-26 were higher, and the PBDIT and PAT were also higher
- Outlook for the current year is challenging on geo-political factors, higher inflation, subdued demand, possible supply-chain disruptions and high energy prices, likely to affect demand and increase costs; medium-to-long-term outlook for India and the industry continues to be bright
